trip.title: Denver ↔ Yellowstone RV Trip
trip.notes: 1,400 included miles (~$0.45/mi over). Return RV full; drop by 10:30 am Wed 15 Jul. Fly 14:05.

days.title: Denver → Casper
days.summary: Pick up RV from Road Bear depot, big grocery shop at Walmart, then drive north on I-25 through Cheyenne and Douglas to Casper. Check in Casper KOA.

days.title: Casper → Fishing Bridge
days.summary: Stop at Lou Taubert Ranch Outfitters in Casper (opens 10 am, closed Mon). Drive US-20/26 west through Shoshoni and stop at Thermopolis Hot Springs State Park. Continue northwest through Worland, Greybull, and Cody before entering Yellowstone via the East Entrance to Fishing Bridge RV Park.

days.title: Yellowstone: Canyon & Hayden Valley
days.fromTo: Fishing Bridge → Canyon Village → Fishing Bridge
days.summary: Day loop north from Fishing Bridge: Mud Volcano, Hayden Valley (bison!), Canyon Village, Artist Point overlook of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone. Return to Fishing Bridge.

days.title: Fishing Bridge → Madison (via geysers)
days.fromTo: Fishing Bridge → West Thumb → Old Faithful → Madison
days.summary: Drive the Grand Loop south to West Thumb Geyser Basin on Yellowstone Lake, then west along the Continental Divide to Old Faithful and the Grand Prismatic Spring (Midway Geyser Basin). End at Madison Campground (dry camping).

days.title: Madison → Cody
days.summary: Morning: Gibbon Falls, Norris Geyser Basin. Drive east through Canyon to Fishing Bridge, then out the East Entrance to Cody. Afternoon: Buffalo Bill Center of the West. Evening: Cody Nite Rodeo, gates 7 pm, rodeo 8 pm.

days.title: Cody → Fort Collins
days.summary: Long drive south: retrace via Greybull, Worland, Thermopolis, Shoshoni, Casper, Douglas, Wheatland, Cheyenne, then south on I-25 to Fort Collins/Lakeside KOA. Fuel up in Cody before leaving — last good-value stop before the park on the return.

days.title: Fort Collins → Denver Airport
days.fromTo: Fort Collins, CO → Denver International Airport
days.summary: Easy morning drive south on I-25. Drop RV at Road Bear depot by 10:30 am. Fly Denver → home at 14:05.

places.name: Casper KOA Journey
places.notes: Night 1. Full hookups, pool, laundry.

places.name: Fishing Bridge RV Park
places.notes: Nights 2 & 3. Full hookups (only hard-sided RVs — bear country). Reservation required.

places.name: Madison Campground
places.notes: Night 4. Dry camping (no hookups). Flush toilets. Bear boxes required.

places.name: Parkway RV Campground
places.notes: Night 5. Walking distance to Buffalo Bill Center and downtown Cody.

places.name: Fort Collins / Lakeside KOA
places.address: 1910 Lakeside Resort Ln, Fort Collins, CO 80524
places.notes: Night 6. Full hookups. Easy I-25 access for final morning.

places.name: Road Bear RV Depot
places.notes: Pickup Day 1 (morning). Return by 10:30 am Day 7. Booking CXF847765-1.

places.name: Walmart Supercenter (big shop)
places.notes: Major grocery and supply run before hitting the road. Stock up for 7 days.

places.name: Lou Taubert Ranch Outfitters
places.notes: Opens 10 am. Closed Mondays. Iconic Western wear store — boots, hats, gear.

places.name: Hot Springs State Park
places.notes: World’s largest mineral hot spring. Free state bathhouse available. Great leg-stretch on long Day 2 drive.

places.name: Buffalo Bill Center of the West
places.notes: World-class Western museum (5 museums in one). Allow 2–3 hours. Open daily.

places.name: Cody Nite Rodeo (Stampede Park)
places.notes: Gates open 7 pm, rodeo starts 8 pm every night June–Aug. Get there early for good seats.

places.name: Hayden Valley
places.notes: Best area in the park for bison herds, grizzly bears, and wolves. Drive slowly and watch the meadows flanking the Yellowstone River.

places.name: Artist Point
places.notes: Classic overlook of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone and Lower Falls. Short walk from parking. Don’t miss it.

places.name: Canyon Village
places.notes: Visitor center, gift shop, gas. Start of the North and South Rim drives to the canyon.

places.name: Mud Volcano
places.notes: Bubbling mud pots and fumaroles. Short boardwalk loop. Sulphurous smell is part of the experience!

places.name: West Thumb Geyser Basin
places.notes: Unique geothermal features right on the shore of Yellowstone Lake. Boardwalk loop ~1 mile.

places.name: Old Faithful
places.notes: Erupts every 60–110 min (avg ~90 min). Check predicted eruption times at the visitor center. Upper Geyser Basin walk is excellent.

places.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
places.notes: Largest hot spring in the US. Rainbow colors best seen from the overlook trail (1 mile RT). Boardwalk gets crowded by 9 am — go early.

places.name: Norris Geyser Basin
places.notes: Hottest, oldest, and most dynamic geyser basin in the park. Two loop trails (Porcelain Basin ½ mi, Back Basin 1.5 mi).

places.name: Denver International Airport (DEN)
places.notes: Flight departs 14:05. Allow 1.5 h at minimum after returning the RV (10:30 drop).

places.name: Horsetooth Reservoir
places.notes: Great reservoir west of Fort Collins with hiking, kayaking, and swimming. Worth a morning stop on Day 7 if time allows.

places.name: New Belgium Brewing
places.notes: Colorado’s largest craft brewery. Tours available; excellent taproom. Day 6 evening wind-down option in Fort Collins.

places.name: Wyoming State Capitol
places.notes: Stunning Romanesque Revival capitol on I-25 corridor. 10-min stop if passing through Cheyenne.

places.name: Cheyenne Frontier Days Old West Museum
places.notes: Celebrates the world’s largest outdoor rodeo. Great carriage collection. Quick stop on I-25 route.

places.name: Terry Bison Ranch
places.address: 51 I-25 Service Rd E, Cheyenne, WY
places.notes: Bison ranch right on I-25 south of Cheyenne. Train ride to see bison up close. Good Day 6 stop heading south.

places.name: Glendo State Park
places.notes: Reservoir on the North Platte River. Good leg-stretch stop on Day 1 or Day 6 along I-25.

places.name: Ayers Natural Bridge
places.notes: Free county park; 30-ft natural stone arch over LaPrele Creek. 12-mile detour off I-25. Picnic area.

places.name: National Historic Trails Interpretive Center
places.notes: Excellent BLM-run museum covering Oregon, California, Mormon, and Pony Express trails through Casper. Worth 1–2 hours.

places.name: Fort Caspar Museum
places.notes: Reconstructed 1865 military fort with living-history exhibits. Near the Platte River Bridge.

places.name: Wind River Canyon Scenic Byway
places.notes: US-20 carves through this spectacular canyon — sheer 2,500-ft walls. You drive through it on Day 2 and Day 6. No detour needed.

places.name: Boysen State Park
places.notes: Reservoir at the mouth of Wind River Canyon. Fishing, boating. Quick stop on US-20 route.

places.name: Wyoming Dinosaur Center
places.notes: One of the top dino museums in the US, with actual dig site tours available. In Thermopolis — easy add-on to the hot springs stop.

places.name: Legend Rock Petroglyph Site
places.notes: Over 300 petroglyphs spanning thousands of years. Off paved road; check road conditions. Day 2 detour.

places.name: Buffalo Bill Dam & Visitor Center
places.notes: Historic arch dam in a spectacular gorge 6 miles west of Cody. Free to visit. Great photo stop entering or leaving Yellowstone.

places.name: Old Trail Town
places.notes: Collection of original 1800s frontier buildings relocated to one site. Cemetery of mountain men and outlaws. Admission ~$8.

places.name: Heart Mountain WWII Interpretive Center
places.notes: Moving museum on the Japanese American internment camp here 1942–45. Between Cody and the park. Allow 1–2 hours.

places.name: Lamar Valley
places.notes: The “American Serengeti” — best wildlife viewing in the lower 48. Bison, wolves, bears, pronghorn. Dawn and dusk are prime time.

places.name: Mammoth Hot Springs
places.notes: Terraced travertine terraces — completely unique geology. Near the north entrance and Albright Visitor Center.

places.name: Tower Fall
places.notes: 132-ft waterfall. Short trail to overlook. Near Tower-Roosevelt junction on the northeast road.

places.name: Gibbon Falls
places.notes: 84-ft falls visible from the road between Madison and Norris. Easy stop on Day 5 morning drive.

places.name: Firehole Canyon Drive (summer swim)
places.notes: One-way scenic drive with a legal swimming hole in the warm Firehole River. Open summer only. Near Madison. Do this on Day 4 or 5.

places.name: Lake Yellowstone Hotel
places.notes: Historic 1891 hotel on Yellowstone Lake. Gorgeous views; even non-guests can walk the lobby and lakefront. Near Fishing Bridge.
